Stone of Immortality / Stone of Intelligence / Stone of Shape / Stone of Afterimage / Stone of Literature / Stone of Echo

The refined knowledge of the kingdom is mainly inscribed into [Stones of Records]. Functions of these six Stones—official approved to this day—are classified based on how they are recorded and how they manifest.

Stone of Immortality: Stores and restores life and time.

Stone of Intelligence: Awakens combat skills, senses, and wisdom.

Stone of Shape: Preserves the structures of objects and their materials.

Stone of Afterimage: Projects memories, scenes, and illusions.

Stone of Literature: Records documents, decrees, and designs.

Stone of Echo: Holds information on voices, sounds, and incantations.

(All Stones of Records must be stored and categorized by grade, in accordance with Article 6 of the Royal Law.)

King Examu’s order to construct sealable gates at the three sanctuaries was delivered in the form of an official letter.

The intention was to establish sanctuaries in three separate regions, securing the spire’s gate once all sanctuaries were sealed. This would ultimately restrain the same type of energy contained within the Stone of Records entrusted by His Majesty.

But I failed to comprehend.

Why would the towering spire require a sealed gate that blocks access from within?

What was the nature of the energy in the Stone of Records that demanded suppression?

I am but a designer.

It was never my place to understand everything.

And yet, His Majesty’s silence seemed to hold something beyond explanation.

...Since that day, I have been haunted by a vague fear that something might one day emerge from that gate.

A beautiful flower once found only in the Higasha Tundra. Though extinct long ago, it remains a symbol of the Sorr. It is said to possess powerful hallucinogenic properties.
When I got too close, it lunged at me with its belly-mouth wide open. Unexpectedly fast. And the saliva this thing spits is so disgusting... I’d never want to set paw on any spot it’s splattered.
It kept out-fighting me whenever I tried to close in. What’s even more frustrating was that magic sphere it summoned. It was always after me.

As I approached, its body swelled and scattered spores in all directions. It felt less like an intelligent attack... and more like a reflex. Whatever combat skills it had honed in life were gone, leaving behind only the instinct to spread infection.
I thought it was harmless when I was close to this thing, but I didn’t want to stay there forever. It doesn’t seem as friendly as it seems.
Up close, I could see that the body was horribly warped, yet scraps of worn clothing still remained. Hard to believe now, but it must have once been an ordinary person who passed through this place.

I braced myself and attacked, but it fell far too easily. I turned to leave—then a sharp sound came from behind. When I looked back, other creatures were crawling out of its fallen body. If possible, it’s best to pass by without engaging.
Now I realize how dreadful the infection is. I must take action to protect everyone from suffering. I know it’s dangerous, but I will stop it.
The infected seem to keep their behaviors from before their mutations. Seeing how agile they are, they must have been elite soldiers in the past.
It caught me off guard by suddenly rolling toward me! That was an unexpected move.
Who would’ve thought an alarm was a signal for an explosion? Better keep an eye on the floor from now on.
It has exceptional pickaxe-throwing skills. For some reason, it looks always mad.
It didn’t show hostility, but there were the infected protecting the juveniles. I found it both interesting and awful that the poison from the hive served as a protective layer.
I heard the village rangers fended off automata that broke in from outside the Kannir Drilling Site a long time ago. Where did those automata come from?
I heard the village rangers fended off automata that broke in from outside the Kannir Drilling Site a long time ago. Where did those automata come from?
The voice from that one cat statue? Honestly, I could barely understand it. At least I caught one word: [kindred]. Could it have been the voice of my ancestor?
He called me a Black Cat. I sensed a mix of emotions from his gaze: confusion, rage, fear, you name it. Although he backed away after our intense fight, he seemed to know my identity.
His last request was simple but serious. I was confused, but he clearly pinned his faith on me.
This entity has been silently repeating its duty. Do the automata know their master is gone?
Its tough shell made every attack useless. The shell can serve as excellent protective gear for village rangers.
I saw its expression as it slowly followed me. ...Frozen in terror, as if that moment had never passed. What exactly happened here...? Why were people gathered in this lab?
It can fly, it’s small and fast, making the fight all the more difficult.
I wonder how it detects me without a hitch. Is it because of the power of magic? Being constantly on the move is the key to dealing with this tough enemy.
If it means protecting everyone I love... I’d return as many times as it takes.
As soon as I touched it, all the crystals on its body shot up at once and rained down on me. Worse, they seemed to change direction midair. It like a swarm of tiny hunters with wills of their own.
I didn’t get hurt, I but lost my mana! I guess that’s one way to defend the castle.
Its tough shell made it nearly impossible to damage the soft flesh beneath. It was far tougher and more tenacious than the Bacantas I’d encountered elsewhere.
Their eyes weren’t just those of common loyal soldiers. Near-blind loyalty and unwavering faith... But for what?
Striking its head while it’s dashing at me causes a tentacle-like [Dark Leech] to fall off. Doing this can knock it down on the spot, but it’s ready to strike back any time.
It was so determined to chase me. Its sharp legs left deep scores, and I could tell how far it had pursued me by watching those marks.

The researcher we thought had fled... returned as something entirely different. Having lost all reason, it lashed out with massive tentacles, tearing apart the facility as it pursued me. I began to suspect that the source of the contamination spreading throughout the lab... might be that very researcher.
The poison smells acidic. I felt dazed and numb when I was exposed to the smell for a while.

I saw familiar names on where stones used to be; they belonged to the Ancients from Aurora Village. It looked like the remaining stones were waiting to be awakened someday. I was heavy-hearted as I lingered in this place.

Thick wood encased its body, making my attacks barely effective. When I shattered the wooden covering, the pustules beneath were exposed—only then did my blows land properly. ...But after some time, the wood grew back, covering its body once more. It felt like a guardian forbidden from ever falling.
The massive tentacles on its back moved first, dragging the body along behind them. It felt like a hollow shell, stripped of its own will. Then it began lashing out, destroying everything around it.
These collectors carried huge sacks on their backs, wearing the same clothes like uniforms. They had no idea they would get infected when they went out to collect Kannics.
The vibration it caused while digging into the ground made rocks fall from above. It had lots of Kannics in its basket as if it collected every single piece in the area.

Only its enormous maw and part of its body emerged above the ground. No one knows how much farther it extends below. Sometimes, when I stare at the ground for too long, I can’t shake the feeling that its body stretches beneath my feet as well.
It knew I was coming, trying to ambush me out of the blue. Watch out for its mandibles; they can clutch anything.
After I hit it, dust erupted and made me glow. Blue light flowed over my body as if alive. Is it just stone powder or some kind of life?
Its back was the safe zone when it fired laser beams! Lucky that there was a cover.
Its long-range drills are a force to be reckoned with.
It doesn’t fly away or come close. Great patience is key to bringing down this monster.
I could tell where it was just by the sound of its clanking and tapping. It tried to stop me from climbing the walls, but it wasn’t too hard to deal with.
A dark shape flickered beneath the water... then in an instant, it surged upward, striking before vanishing below again. When it leaps out, that’s the moment to land a decisive blow.
It looked unstable. One strong impact flung it away, but as soon as it regained its balance, it started chasing me again.
It looks like a better wall climber than I am.
That secretion was unimaginably explosive. Small as it was, when it detonated it shook the surroundings. What’s its inside made of to produce such a deadly weapon?
It falls when it runs into walls, and that’s the perfect moment to strike. The more I look at it, the more curious I am about what it’s made of to be that tough.
It looked different from the rest of the infected—in appearance, aggressiveness, almost everything. It makes me believe there’s a varying degree of mutation.
Every part is mismatched. Metal plates of unknown origin, crudely fused together... It looks dangerous just to get close... Can it even be recovered? Or... does that no longer matter?
After I picked up the brooch, something strange started happening. The tentacles blocking my path suddenly sank into the ground as I approached... As if they were afraid.
It’s utterly wrecked, but I remember seeing one of these at the Kannir Drilling Site. It must have been common, used in many places. Every time I see the Ancients’ technology, I’m impressed.
Sharp toes for effective wall climbing, small frame for easier navigation.
The automaton guard captain was dangerously agile. Was it because of its small size and wings?
I guess engravers are natural wielders of magic. I almost let my guard down when they suddenly disappeared right before my eyes.
The electricity is back in full supply after I turned the switch on! These machines look complicated... Does it supply power to other places?
Sharp weapons on both limbs. I have no idea what these tools were initially used for, or what these workers could possibly be doing here.
Its eyes suddenly glow before it leaps out of the dark. I could easily dodge it with extra caution. Still, it almost caught me by surprise at first.
Its agility and sharp spear make it even more dangerous. The best countermeasure is to dodge the moment it rushes in.
The Owl Tribe was here too. They seem to have honed skills other than handling the Stones of Records.
The Owl Tribe was here too. They seem to have honed skills other than handling the Stones of Records.
Extremely sensitive to external stimuli. It gave me lots of trouble until the end.
It ferociously springs out at anyone or anything once it detects movement. It appears to be driven by nothing but hostility because of the infection.
I almost mistook it for a corpse because it wasn’t moving. Those sharp spikes made for perfect replacements for its weapons.

Its movements were relentless. When I drew close, it lashed out with vines, trying to ensnare me. If I created distance, it spat out grotesque plant growths and continued the pursuit. It felt less like a fight... and more like being hunted.

This infected wandered aimlessly through the corridors, spreading contamination wherever it went. It looked slow and sluggish, so I let my guard down and approached. ...In that instant, its head snapped toward me—and it lunged at incredible speed.
It appears to be the strongest infected in the area... Could it be the one that caused the spikes to grow on the collectors’ bodies?
This creature seems to rest after a leap. Maybe it consumes a lot of energy while jumping.

It often remains perfectly still in the darkness, so more than once I found myself unknowingly stepping into the range of those horrific spines. That’s why you must always move carefully, keeping a close watch on your surroundings.
I think I saw this one at the Kannir Drilling Site. Maybe they needed more workers.
This flier seems to chase its target relentlessly. Luckily, it wasn’t too tough to bring down.
There were numbers on their clothes, without any pattern between them.
I will never forget your favor. May Nagaraja’s grace be with you.
People here seemed to have repurposed old automata. I’ve never seen anything like this before.
The air here is unusually silent and heavy. The walls have withstood the test of time, still standing firm without a single scratch. What could this column of sealing devices be holding inside?

When moving, it stays very close to the surface. But just before attacking, it always burrows deeper underground and vanishes completely. In those moments, you must watch your footing carefully and stay alert to where the attack may come from.
I was horrified. Those leeches appear to have seized full control of that soldier.
It will never stop bugging me! I get quickly exhausted because these flies keep coming at me.
This thing was unlike anything I’d seen before. Its sheer size was so overwhelming, all I could think about was running away...
I caught a glimpse of that cold gaze beneath the hat in a fleeting moment. Those were the eyes of someone pure of heart.
From its jabs, I could tell it was a seasoned soldier. I had to stay wary of its reach during the fight.
I thought it was just a simple spell, but it felt like my mind was being pulled away. What was really dangerous was the intent behind it, not just the chant...
At first, I froze at the noise these things produced. Later, that same sound was how I knew they were closing in on me in the dark.
It waited in ambush on the ceiling, completely hidden. That wasn’t the work of ordinary stealth... Could it be magic?

It hung motionless from the ceiling, watching its surroundings through countless eyes. Every so often, all of those eyes would turn toward the same place at once... In those moments, it felt as though someone was looking out at the world through them.
I saw children who came to collect Kannics turned into the infected. They appear to be floating due to their small frames, but why would they come to such a dangerous place?
This unit had strength to match its massive size. Even after taking it down, I had to be careful. Its unstable head was still a threat.
I thought its transparent body drifting in the air was beautiful. But I was wrong when it suddenly lunged at me.
It never stopped walking along the golden thread. What amazed me was that the thread didn’t snap even though this thing looked quite heavy.
Is life in the Higasha Tundra so harsh that they resort to stealing just to survive? I hope things get better for them in Aurora Village.

Its strength and speed were threatening, but above all, its movements were precise. Even the underwater environment seemed no hindrance to them. It seems the combat techniques carved into their bodies through long training still remain.
Its swing was so powerful, it even produced a shockwave! It could take a serious beating, so I avoided striking recklessly.

...I cannot conclude whether my decision was right. The powerful crystallization magic sealed His Majesty at the cost of my physical form, leaving only this forlorn soul. May a hero guide His Majesty and the kingdom back to the path of light...

May 1
I saw you for the first time on an ultrasound today.
You’re still so tiny, but I can already feel you there.
I have white fur, and your father has black fur...
Who will you take after?
As thanks for gifting me the [Seed of Healing], I present this portrait of you. May the seed soon bloom, and may the world be cleansed by flowers as beautiful as you.

[The Golden Spirit Wolf] Enma. Infiltrate Aurora Village and gather the pieces of Aisare’s Stone by any means necessary. Those weak fools, crushed by shortages and fear of infection, will come to firmly believe that the cure is inscribed within those stones. Use your medical knowledge to feign helping them and earn their trust. And when Aisare’s Stone is finally completed... our long-awaited wish shall at last be fulfilled.

The royal court saw his efforts to spread engraving as a threat. His honor was stripped away, and the Imprint School was dismantled. In his later years, Nagaraja foresaw the Day of Ruin that would come after his death. On the prophesied day, his followers inscribed Nagaraja into the Stone of Life to awaken him once more.

Security systems linked to the Watcher will immediately neutralize any detected intruders. The emitted beams can cause fatal injuries. Unauthorized access is strictly prohibited. Personnel assigned to secure zones must adhere to designated schedules and routes at all times.

Grande, congratulations on your pregnancy! I look better in this photo, but I’ll give it to you.
P.S. That brooch His Majesty gave you really suits you.

Your Grace, in the end, you protected what mattered most to you. Though we lost so much, the path we walked was never in vain. Now I can finally rest easy and be reunited with His Majesty and our comrades.

No matter how beautifully one dresses up his failure as a tale, the outcome does not change. I refuse to witness the same failure again. That is why I neither deny prophecy nor place blind faith in it. I simply will not allow reckless judgment based on borrowed words. I judge only by results.
I don’t remember the last words I shared with him. One thing I never forget—our pawsteps always in the same pace...

Nagaraja’s bestial transformation was not an ascension toward a primordial form. It was a path that separated flesh from soul, becoming a beast to halt the end. With his enlarged body, he devoured countless infected and held his ground until the very end.

I do not see Nagaraja’s prophecy as a single, predetermined ending. It is not an answer, but a question left behind for this world. I do not seek to answer that question. I merely watch to see what outcomes each individual choice will bring.
Is flight relying on apparatus really flying? Or are some tribes just trying to forget the fact that they can’t fly? Either way, I understand how they feel. Hoot, hoot!

What if sealing technology were integrated into a shield? The result would be an impregnable defense, the pinnacle of craftsmanship. This is not just a shield, but a barrier embodying the royal court’s unwavering resolve to repel any attack.

Do not resist the flow of water. Surrender yourself, and become one with the current. Only those unbound by form may cross the rapids, and to those who dissolve themselves into the flow, no threat shall reach.

An alternative to a bug zapper? That’s an idea no one has ever thought of. It might prove effective if its output is reduced. Nevertheless, every tool has its intended purpose, and misusing it could dishonor its inventor.

I prayed that someone would one day appear and bring light back to this world... And at last, you have set me free. Then this darkness, too, shall soon fade. Hope will bloom once more, not only in this forest, but throughout the entire world.
Strigine lightbringers, we were able to save more souls thanks to your research.

The world is moving forward once again. This child has inherited the will Your Majesty left behind. I have no regrets left now. Your Majesty... I only hope that this time, we can finish the conversation we never had.
The battle we fought alongside countless comrades was not in vain after all. At last, I can lay everything to rest. Helena... do not be bound by the past. Walk your own path.
On that day, when the battle was too evenly matched to decide a victor, we split the medallion granted to the greatest warrior in two. Though he was called a traitor, I still cannot forget his name.

The structure has been reinterpreted based on machinery used at the drilling site. The goal is to maintain output efficiency while enabling more precise operations. Automata technology remains not fully understood, but combined with Origin’s technology, its potential applications would expand greatly.
His Majesty met his end while attempting to contain the infection from reaching the surface. All I could do was seal and preserve his body in crystal, safe from contamination.
Ugh... I wish I had an icemaker. It’s such a pain preparing ice every day.
The Kannic shockwave this creature unleashes isn’t caused by mere impact, but by a resonant phenomenon that mysteriously echoes through the underground Kannir vein, rapidly crystallizing it.

I crafted this coffin to confine the seeds of chaos prevalent in this world. It may be sealed only with the Silver Claw and unlocked only with the Golden Claw. Should this law be broken, chaos will consume the kingdom.

The sap flowing from this sacred tree rarely solidifies, and it is said to transform into a substance imbued with mysterious power and medicinal properties. Within the tree’s interior, tribe members trained themselves to surrender to the flow of water, overcoming the fears within their hearts.

This spore appears to be parasitizing other plants. It seems to borrow the form of its host to move, hunt, and spread infection. Hoot-hoot... rather than an independent lifeform, it resembles a reproductive organ born of the infected forest itself.

It feels wonderful to have a friend to share this kind of joy with.
Thank you, Iedart. And...
You’ll be someone special to this child as well.

Very strange indeed. Its green glow is so intense that you can never miss it from miles away. Clearly, there is a reason for us to collect this at all costs, but we can never shrug off the threat lurking behind the glistening pile. Should it be considered dazzling, or dangerous?

Paper decays and memories fade. But stone endures, bearing eternal witness. That is why we chose the Stones of Records. We engraved upon them every fragment of knowledge—what we saw, felt, and heard. Thus, this Archive was founded, built on the belief that a better future must stand upon an unforgettable past.
Storing and releasing poisonous gas at will... It seems to be a way of evolution to survive extreme conditions. Hehe, isn’t that amazing?

The Jibanam tribe... just hearing that name makes my blood boil. After leaving the tribe, I did whatever it took to survive. I endured endless training to make it this far. But I won’t settle for this. Just remembering those painful days still makes it hard to breathe...
Wise owls, battles aren’t just contests of strength. We will prove it.
This supports my theory that the resins have a network of their own. They slowly ferry bones and corpses, producing and dropping more resin to contaminate the surroundings.

Poppos are said to respond keenly to the emotions of other living beings, possessing an empathic ability that soothes anxiety and fear. Within the Jibanam Tree, they are believed to help those who fear water adapt to its flow.

The Blood ball is a forbidden medicinal ingredient. The act of making it, sacrificing life itself, is a felony that threatens the very foundation of the kingdom. Though the accused sought only to save their child, such disruption of order cannot be taken lightly. Thus, the sentence is passed: eternal confinement within the Mirror, to repent perpetually.

Pathetic imitators.
True creation begins only in the hands of Murant.

An inventor and owner of [Gatorware]. Managing the business that has been passed down for three generations, he is deeply interested in artifacts from Elord Castle. He is dexterous in turning his brilliant ideas into reality.

A programmer at [Gatorware]. Working in the business that has been passed down for three generations, he has a profound interest in artifacts from Elord Castle. He is delving into this world with his unique approach.
A researcher who collects the shattered pieces of [Aisare’s Stone]. She is conducting her research to restore this stone that contains the knowledge for a plague cure.
An abandoned, shut-down construct of automata. Heavily damaged to the point its inner parts are exposed. Even a small impact may make it collapse.
A tribal hunter parasitized by thorned vines. It attacks using the thorny growth sprouting from its back and releases mutated plant matter formed within its body to relentlessly pursue its prey.
An infected miner battered with years of labor.

An infected entity that spreads contamination throughout the facility by hurling fragments of its own infected tissue. It exhibits a common mutation observed among lab-infected entities, with massive tentacles protruding from its back. It displays extreme aggression toward any uninfected individuals that approach.
Using the Stone of Records imbued with the power of lightning, this infected mage fends off intruders.
An infected soldier. Extends spikes that have overgrown on its body due to infection.
An infected pilgrim. It unleashes all of its skills that used to be controlled by its self-discipline and kindness.
An infected facility worker. It charges toward a target with its sharp horn and stout build.
An infected facility worker. Clinging to high walls, it swoops down on its prey.
An infected facility worker. It aggressively lunges at its target.
An infected facility worker. Despite wielding a massive, man-sized pickaxe, it can move swiftly.
An infected strigine engraver that wields a chisel as its weapon of choice.
An infected strigine artisan. Hurls magic attacks using mana infused into automata.
An infected spearman that lunges at its enemies using a floating cloak.
An infected spearman that adeptly attacks from a distance with a long spear.
With a huge mouth gaping from its abdomen, this infected creature either gnaws its prey with razor-sharp teeth or spits explosive goo.
A tribal warrior whose body has mutated due to infection. Trained to fight even underwater, their once formidable physique has fused with plant tissue, transforming into an even more resilient form.
Having undergone mutations for a long time, this infected monster now has razor-sharp claws and spikes.
A facility worker with deformed body parts due to severe infection. It uses its twisted limbs as a blade and a shield.
The skull of [Nagaraja], the magnificent Mythical Creature revered by the Serpent tribe. Even after his death, his teachings have been passed down for generations.

A mysterious spiritual device resembling a gigantic clock. It is believed to possess the power to send those chosen by the Ancestors back through time by reversing the flow of fate. At its center is a socket, seemingly designed to hold a specific object.
An evolved form of a Dark Leech. It leaps over a long distance to gore a target.
A roaming biologist studying dark resins and Dark Leeches. She is well-versed in failproof but bizarre ways of surviving in this infected-infested world.
The smallest individual of Dark Leeches. Hanging from ceilings, it swoops down on its prey.
A stealth-type infected that burrows through the floor of the Black Canyon. When prey enters its territory, it approaches unseen beneath the ground, striking from behind out of the darkness.
A strigine engraver on apprenticeship. He strives diligently to follow the path of his esteemed teacher.
The Stone of Records engraved with the wisdom of the ancient. A subtle blue glow surrounds the edges of the carved symbols.
A magical transportation device invented by Vanrion, an ancestor from the ancient kingdom of Elord. You can travel through Vanrion’s Gates.
A sculpture in the form of Kelgard, an ancestor of the ancient kingdom of Elord. You can detect Kannium from this statue, a crucial material for enhancing your Claw.
A researcher of the Engraved Formulas left behind by the Ancients. He strives to restore the forgotten Engraving technique by deciphering their enigmas and completing the formulas.
A mollusk that floats in place for long periods. The adhesive substance it spits clings to surfaces and, after a delay, releases explosive energy.
A mutated plant that floats through the air, tracking living beings. Upon death, it detonates the spores accumulated within, spreading infection to its surroundings.
An ancient, floating predator. On spotting prey, its head reshapes into a sharp form before lunging.
One of the Six Champions and mentor to King Odz. When Odz was wounded in battle at the Sealed Spire, he sealed the king in crystal. Since then, he has guarded the Kannir Sanctuary in spirit form.

Once a member of the ancient Yellow Cats. He was sealed within Jayma’s Dungeon for attempting to achieve immortality by recording his own life at the cost of others. After being imprisoned within a Sealing Sphere for countless ages, endless solitude and hatred transformed him into a monster that spreads plague and brings ruin to the world.

A site for a fierce battle in the past. White ash rising in clouds and dark resins covering the ruins create a clear yet peculiar contrast. Crumbled structures and abandoned weapons hint at how intense the battle was.
A confluence of gentle winds that swept through the chambers and tunnels of the mines. The wind grew much more violent due to years of mining and natural erosion.
A photograph found in Grande’s laboratory. It shows Grande looking shy, while Iedart appears surprised.
A photograph found in Grande’s laboratory. It captures the moment she first saw the fetus through an ultrasound.
Climbing walls freely with sharp claws and moving in the shadows, this infected cheetah can throw its enemies into disarray using its swift movements.
An imposing keeper wielding a golden magic shield. Crafted using a special method, this shield cannot be pierced by ordinary means.
Born in the Higasha Tundra, Cain broke into Elord Castle in search of the Golden Claw. With his agility and fierce swordsmanship, he can drive his adversaries into a corner.
A form of automata designed for mining raw materials for Stones of Records along with Kannics. Its forehead drill can easily crush even the hardest rocks.
A form of automata designed for mining raw materials for Stones of Records. Effective for collecting exposed ores.
A form of automata designed for mining raw materials for Stones of Records. It uses small yet sophisticated drills to detect ores buried deep underground.

A zone equipped with devices used to restore what has been inscribed in the Stone of Records. The restoration process consumes immense energy, and the system appears to use Kannir as its power source.

An altar used to restore what has been inscribed within the Stone of Records. Through ritual, the power of dark spirits is drawn forth and used as the energy required for restoration. Countless sacrifices destined to become dark spirits are required for this ritual.

The Owl tribe has exclusively supervised this blue bedrock area for generations, the site for mining raw materials for the Stone of Records. Gales sweep through every corner of this quarry due to its geographical characteristics.

The Owl tribe has exclusively supervised this blue bedrock area for generations, the site for mining raw materials for the Stone of Records. Gales sweep through every corner of this quarry due to its geographical characteristics.
A tribal fighter overtaken by parasitic spores. It swells the pustules formed across its body and disperses spores into the air, spreading infection throughout the area.

A mysterious stone that contains Memory Fragments. Echostones are said to exist beyond the flow of time. They may suddenly appear where none existed before, only to vanish without a trace. Even newly discovered Echostones bear the marks of centuries—if not millennia—of weathering, leaving no one able to tell how long they have truly been there.
A flying creature with extensive wings. It marks its territory by periodically dropping poison droplets.
A massive cliff whose bottom cannot be seen. Souls continuously rise from below and flow into the machinery above. It is believed that bodies from across the Higasha Tundra were disposed of here.
An emergency shutdown device for violent automata. It triggers an explosion upon receiving a certain degree of impact. Ineffective against organic lifeforms.
An amphibious automaton unit constructed from scraps. Capable of discharging powerful bursts of electricity forward.
A set of automata assembled from old parts. Despite its rough construction, it doesn’t break easily, even under heavy impact.

An infected entity that carries Corpse Plunderers within its body. Most of its form has collapsed due to infection, retaining only the bare minimum functions needed to harbor its parasites. As a result, its movements are slow and unstable, and even a light impact will cause it to collapse, spilling the Corpse Plunderers inside.
A corpse preserved by crystallization, which is an extremely rare phenomenon.
A venomous fly that spits poison to keep enemies at bay.
Appears to be the same species as the Lis found in other regions. Its bizarre appearance is marked by multiple sharp eyes protruding from its body.
A merchant selling a variety of antiques. Countless scars and loss of vision hint at the hardships he might have endured in the past.
With her attentive and bubbly nature, Lara runs a tea house, serving various teas to uplift the villagers. She is always on the lookout for quality tea ingredients.
Clad in a solid shell, this creature usually burrows into the ground out of innate fear. But then, it bursts to the surface out of surprise upon hearing footsteps.
The large corporation [Origin] established this facility for ancient technology research. It appears to have been built recently. Currently, only a few machines are operating on emergency power.
An infected axeman. Its attacks are as devastating as the sheer size of its axe.
A hive of Poisonflies. It is provided with feed to nurture Juvenile Poisonflies.
It is not mature yet, but big enough to fly around.
Easy to throw off due to its slowness.
An ancient creature bearing a razor-edged Kannic crystal on its back. It leaps high into the air and releases a Kannic shockwave on impact with the ground.
An evolved form of the Lis adapted to dark environments. Its organs can detect life in darkness. It feeds chiefly on the corpses of those who perished in the shadows.
A naturally formed cave with clean water. Many plants grow in this humid habitat, and thanks to its abundant resources, various creatures frequent or even inhabit this cave.

Sorron’s hidden cavern, where grotesque plants are cultivated using the blood and souls of the dead as nourishment. Once sprouted, the seeds endlessly propagate, spreading thorns of death that corrupt and destroy everything around them. To accelerate the downfall of the underground world, Sorron deceived survivors into believing these cursed seeds were [Seeds of Healing] capable of purifying the contaminated underground, spreading them far and wide.

Designed for mining Kannir buried underground, this facility appears to have been built recently. The Kannir gas leaking from many areas of the facility is toxic, making it deadly for inattentive visitors.
A sanctuary built in the past in gratitude to nature. Abandoned and exposed to Kannir energy for ages, much of its structure is slowly crystallizing.
One of the sanctuaries established long ago in gratitude for nature. Embodying the distinctive blue hue from the cerulean bedrock, it also emanates the potent power of seals.

In ages past, this sanctuary was erected within the Moss Cave in gratitude to nature. Built to honor the headwaters that flow throughout the kingdom, the place is permeated with a tranquil and gentle aura of water.
Despite being the only passage to the surface world, it was sealed in the distant past. No one knows how to undo the seal now.
This monster hovers in one place until it spots a target.
An altar hidden deep within the Aphotic Marsh. A place where chosen sacrifices are bound and offered as living tributes.

A Deathworm found within the Aphotic Marsh. It possesses far greater vitality than specimens found elsewhere. Its anatomy is also considerably more complete, suggesting that Deathworms from other regions may have originated from these.

A Bacanta found within the Aphotic Marsh. Its sharp eyes are a trait shared by many infected creatures in this region. It is believed that an original specimen lies at the root of this mutation, and that all infected creatures in the Aphotic Marsh may have diverged from it.

An infected warrior of the Jibanam tribe encountered at the entrance to the Water Sanctuary. Possessing a massive frame and overwhelming strength, it blocks those who attempt to enter the sanctuary with arms warped by infection.

A photograph found in Murant’s laboratory. A group photo taken to commemorate the launch of the project during the founding of the Origin Laboratory. The faces of every researcher except Murant have been defaced.

A mysterious stele that keeps the records of life and time and restores them. As the magnum opus of ancient Elord technology, no one knows how to use it.

A mysterious substance believed to be crystallized memories left behind within the gaps of time. It is said to contain everything from memories long forgotten to memories yet to come. A glowing ore formed from the petrified scales shed by a Mythical Creature’s corpse. On impact, fine fluorescent dust billows out, briefly illuminating the area.
A severely infected carnivorous plant. When someone approaches, it closes its mouth to protect itself.

An infected entity that lies in silence within the darkness, waiting for someone to approach. Once a target is detected, it slowly gives chase. When it reaches its prey, it raises the sharp spines covering its body and attacks.

A massive monument erected to record the history and achievements of the Elord royal family. The silver and gold ornaments surrounding it have long been regarded as symbols of the royal lineage. The last king of the Elord Kingdom. To prevent contamination from spreading to the surface, he sealed the gates of the spire and fought until his final breath. Though preserved through Kannic crystallization by Dotiman, it is believed he awoke once more when the Sanctuary seals weakened.

An experimental unit developed by the Origin Laboratory based on Elord Kingdom’s Automata technology. It was used to transport large equipment, materials, and delicate experimental devices within the lab.

A classified underground zone constructed by the order of King Examu the first king of Elord Kingdom. Accessible only by the royal blood, it is currently sealing anything that can threat the kingdom’s order and peace.
A place established for commemorating the Six Champions. Only one statue remains destroyed for a mysterious reason.
A sacred hall where the stone statues of all Elord Kingdom’s monarchs stand in solemn rows. Only those of royal blood—or of equal qualification—are allowed to enter.

An infected entity identified as a lead researcher of the Origin Laboratory. Despite infection, it appears to retain unstable traces of consciousness. Notably, tentacles have emerged from its back.

Unidentified tentacles found in heavily contaminated areas. They emerge as if growing from cracks in the ground or gaps within structures, each one constantly writhing as though it were alive.
Automata of various sizes were produced and repaired here. The workshop was once busy with robust manufacturing, but visitors have since stopped coming.
Located in the far eastern reaches of the kingdom, the people of this snowfield region have developed a distinct culture.

An infected entity found within the kingdom’s canals. It typically lurks beneath the surface before ambushing targets above the water. Among survivors of its attacks, it has become feared under the name [Terror Beneath the Water].

A designated chamber prepared for the kingdom’s potential crisis. Stones of Immortality are stored here, embodying information on the lives of the Ancients. Traces of Origin’s efforts to transport these stones, along with the corporation’s hauling machines, still remain.
[Jayma] the sage invented this powerful sealing device under the order of King Examu the first king. It was later named the Golden Sealing Sphere and hidden deep underground.
Captain of the royal automaton guards. It continues to protect Elord Castle, awaiting the never-returning king.

An automaton assistant in the boutique. It produces and weaves golden thread to craft special fabrics for the royal court.

A type of mineral that serves as both the source of energy and currency in this world. its distinctive green glow can be observed from a distance.

The entire canyon feels like a single massive corpse, lying dormant in silence.

The kingdom’s headwater source, located deep within the Moss Cave. During the outbreak, the warriors of Saemo’s tribe defended this place to the very end. Even now, it continues to supply clean water throughout the kingdom.

A photograph found in Iedart’s laboratory. It shows Iedart joyfully embracing Grande.

A cavern with geological formations unlikely to have formed naturally. Analysis has revealed the highest contamination levels recorded in any known region. Black sludge generated throughout the underground world appears to ultimately flow here, covering the entire area in contamination.
Assimilated with Dark Leeches, this watcher, infected during the war, can enter and leave dark resin pits.

An assassin who was infected during the war. Even after losing its mind, it can still move with stealth and agility.

Having a unique preference for narrow alleys, this creature hangs down its tentacles to detect its prey.

A chronicler of Jibanam descent who resides by the waters near the Jibanam Tree. A survivor of the outbreak, he continues his own research in hopes of restoring the forest.

A small lifeform that once lived in symbiosis with the Jibanam Tree. Known to move in groups and possess exceptional empathic abilities. Its flexible and elastic body structure allows it to absorb or redirect physical impact.
Once a symbol of a thriving civilization, this massive, aurulent castle sits at the heart of the kingdom. Three towering spires embodying the shape of claws rise into the sky.

Mined stones used to be processed here. A blue stone, seemingly inert, transforms into a [Stone of Records] through the effort of strigine artisans to become recordable. The royal council then determines what this empty stone will contain.
A mass of dark resins on the ceiling. Bones and nameless organs are mixed within, causing a lifelike writhing.
The apex predator of the Kannir food chain. It remains harmless so long as its territory is not violated. If you must approach, do so at your own risk.

A Cabitz dealer. Being the last survivor of the war, she remains on the ruinous battlefield, honoring her fallen companions in her own way.

A piece of brooch holding vital force. One piece alone can’t do anything. You might want to collect more of these.
I bought this from some well-spoken traveler, but I can’t find any use for it. Take it if you want, but it won’t come cheap. It cost me a fortune to get my paws on it.

I don’t know what they’re used for, but there’s something unusual about the aura they give off, so I’ve been buying them whenever I find one. Strangely, whenever I hold one... I’m overcome with emotions I can’t quite explain—longing, regret... It’s as if I’m meeting someone I forgot long ago.

Defenders of the kingdom used this healing marble. It was reduced to debris, shattered in the flames of a fierce battle. If you can gather the pieces... who knows? Perhaps a little of its ancient power can be restored.
Knock it off. This isn’t for sale.

I found this while investigating beneath the Western Bridge of Elord Castle for my records. If you possess the other fragment, it may be able to store even more vital force.
Even after the world changed like this, the devices powered by Kannir have not ceased functioning. If you need a long-lasting power source for complex machinery, nothing is more reliable than this.

Our tribe has used this substance in sacred rituals since ancient times. We believe it allows us to receive the memories of old, commune with the spirits of our ancestors, and learn from their wisdom. I’ve also heard that, long ago in Elord Castle, a device was created using this very substance to restore lost memories and forgotten records.
This relic allows your claw strikes to knock enemies farther away, giving you more room to recover.

This is a map I compiled myself while moving through the Moss Cave. I’ve marked the vanished paths and newly formed ones as accurately as possible. It took quite some time to finish, since I had to draw it while on the run. The terrain has changed so drastically that I had to verify everything again.
Carry it, and Spiones will see you as a giant nest and protect you from external forces. It holds a significant research value as the first case of artifactizing a lifeform.

A fascinating object with an uncanny aura. I’ve found stones containing these fragments in many different places, yet none of those locations have anything in common. It’s almost as though the stones choose where they appear...
This artifact holds the tenacity of fallen warriors. When you wear it, their will infuses you with immense power when you are at the brink of death.
According to a royal engineer, installing this on a Vanrion’s Gate opens a route to a Stone of Immortality. But remember: returning only lets you catch your breath. The fight is far from over.
Come back once you can clear walls the way the Irbes unit does.
This artifact increases the wearer’s Health. Particularly useful when you prefer dangerous melee combat. You might not need it at all if you are confident in your dodging skills.
This item holds the king’s resolve to defend his realm. A final pledge for us survivors. Only the rightful successor to his will may possess it.
Carry this with you, and your ancestors will help you in the most desperate moment. It’s okay to seek their help if you face a barrier.

It’s a type of key used in the kingdom. Fashioned after the sun, it was only designed for magic doors. The sun has long symbolized the kingdom’s will. I wonder if the survivors still understand its significance.
It’s a Kannir energy catalyst designed by King Kelgard himself. It’s stored in a special container, but handle it with care. Kannir is extremely unstable.

I brewed this in the traditional way Rotri told me... But wow, there were so many steps involved. I’ve never done this before, so I’m not sure if it works. I’d like to test it, but you’d have to be dead first to be brought back! I’ve got no stomach to drink it. Besides, it smells so awful... makes me almost pass out even before taking a sip.
Drink this tea, and you’ll feel like you’re drenched in Mana! The subtle scent of soil is what makes this Moss Flower Tea so special. A purr-fect pick-me-up!

This tea is brewed from a flower called the Dreamspirit Flower. It was said to bloom only in the cold eastern lands, and its fragrance would make you drowsy and leave you in a dreamlike haze. In severe cases, people would even experience hallucinations so vivid they could no longer tell dreams from reality. The interesting part is that people didn’t actually drink the tea—they steeped the flower in hot water and inhaled only its aroma. Of course, the flower is extinct now, so nobody can even see it anymore... I’d love to know what it smelled like at least once!

I prepared the Dreamspirit Flower tea the traditional way. I only caught a faint whiff of it, but my eyelids immediately grew heavy and I felt incredibly sleepy. Maybe those stories about seeing hallucinations so vivid you can’t tell dreams from reality aren’t exaggerated after all. I should really try breathing in the aroma properly before bed sometime. Still, the scent was wonderful. It felt like a faded childhood memory suddenly resurfacing, gently tugging at something deep inside my heart. I’ll keep some steeped and warm, so feel free to stop by and enjoy it anytime!

They say this was a drink favored by the researchers who worked at the Origin Laboratory. Apparently, it relieves fatigue and sharpens the mind when consumed. For those working through the night, it was considered essential. If you happen to find any of these [Beans], could you bring them to me? The ingredients can’t be obtained anymore... but I’d still like to recreate that flavor at least once.

That subtle bitter and nutty aroma... it’s definitely unlike any other tea. Drinking it makes your mind feel clearer and your body lighter. Maybe this was the reason the researchers could work day and night without stopping. ...I tried it once myself, but I ended up having trouble sleeping that night. Maybe... it’s just not the right drink for me.

Rotri said it’s an ancient magic tea that can even bring back the dead... I mean, come on. If that kind of tea is real, why would we need hospitals? Still, I thought a legendary tale like this might catch visitors’ interest for a bit.

I brew this tea from Fuyuri fruits. Easterners enjoy this tea to warm themselves and regain energy. You’ll definitely want a cup of Fuyuri tea if you wanna keep yourself warm and energetic throughout the day!

I brew this tea from Fuyuri fruits. They’re very rare since they only grow in the cold east region. Easterners enjoy this tea to warm themselves and regain energy. If you ever visit the east, can you please get me some? I’m almost out of stock!
